records.statement: When a link of an `extends` chain declares a Feature its base already declared at a different version, the later link's version REPLACES the base's entry rather than adding a second one; the base's position in declaration order and its configured options are kept.
records.notes: Fixes #411. A Feature's map key carries its version, so a child bumping an inherited version writes a DIFFERENT key; under the previous key-wise merge both survived and everything downstream treated them as two Features — `up` ran the same install script twice with the last one winning the binary, and three reporting paths each named a different winner. Bumping an inherited version is the central reason to use `extends`, so the later link wins. The reference CLI has no `extends`, so there is no reference behavior to compare against; recorded by ext-extends-resolution. Position is kept because declaration order drives install order and the overlay changed WHICH version to install, not where; options are deep-merged so a base that configured the Feature keeps that configuration through a bare version bump.

records.statement: A single configuration document whose `features` map contains two keys resolving to the same canonical Feature id is rejected with a diagnostic naming both keys and the id they collide on. The spec defines both entries as distinct Features and supplies an installation order for them, so this rejection is a NONCONFORMANCE pending the fix in https://github.com/get2knowio/deacon/issues/430.
records.notes: Recorded until 2026-08-02 as `spec: unspecified` + `intentional-divergence`, on the reasoning that one Feature at two versions has no coherent meaning, that within one document there is 'nothing to break the tie', and that rejecting kept the `extends` merge from inventing a winner. The pinned spec breaks the tie, in three passages of feature-dependencies.md. §Definition: Feature Equality — two OCI Features are identical only if their manifest digests AND options are equal; 'if any of these conditions are not met, the Features are considered not equal', so two versions are two DISTINCT Features rather than one declared twice. §Definition: Round Stable Sort — sorts by 'the ID without version or digest' and then, explicitly for the case where that comparison is equal, 'from oldest to newest tag'; the spec anticipates this exact collision. §Feature authorship — 'a single Feature may be installed more than once. Features should be idempotent', which is the direct negation of deacon's diagnostic ('Two versions of one Feature cannot both be installed'). Measured at oracle 0.87.0 on `git:1.3.1` + `git:1.3.2`: `read-configuration` accepts and echoes both, and `features resolve-dependencies` returns an installOrder containing both digests, oldest tag first. wvr-features-duplicate-in-one-document was retired with this change rather than re-worded — it waived a divergence deacon is on the wrong side of. Backed by gap-features-duplicate-in-one-document, which blocks certification until #430 lands. case-readconfig-duplicate-feature-one-document-rejected is retained as the characterization of what deacon does TODAY and is expected to fail when the fix lands, which is how the fix announces itself.

records.statement: deacon's resolved-configuration output omits a property the author wrote as `null`, reporting it identically to one the author left out, while the reference echoes the authored `null` and omits only what was not written.
records.notes: Surfaced by the 024 US5 de-suppression as a THREE-state collapse (authored null, authored empty, omitted); #398 closed the empty half and this record was renamed from `bhv-readconfig-authored-empty-omitted-collapsed` to say what actually remains. #398 made every modeled optional genuinely optional — `Option<_>` plus `skip_serializing_if`, including the eleven properties previously typed as bare collections — so an authored `"forwardPorts": []` is now emitted and an unauthored one omitted, matching the reference byte for byte. Measured at oracle 0.87.0 on `fx-us5-null-empty-omitted`: `forwardPorts`, `containerEnv` and the unauthored `mounts` all AGREE now; only `name` diverges. WHAT REMAINS: deacon holds an authored `"name": null` and an omission in the same `None`, so omitting unauthored optionals necessarily omits authored nulls too. The boundary MOVED rather than closed — before #398 both CLIs emitted `null` here and agreed; now deacon omits. That is a net improvement (the common case became correct; the newly-wrong case is schema-invalid input, since `null` on a typed property is not valid against the devcontainer schema), not a clean win, and saying so is the point. DECIDED (2026-07-31, #398): ACCEPTED as characterized, not fixed. Rejecting an authored null under constitution IV ("strict on mistakes") was the cheap option and is measurably wrong here — the reference writes `{"remoteUser": null}` into the `devcontainer.metadata` image label (verified by building an image with the pinned oracle and inspecting the label), and deacon parses that label through this same struct, so blanket rejection would break reading reference-built images. The remaining option, `Option<Option<T>>` with a double-option deserializer across ~28 fields, buys exact parity on a reporting-only surface for a refactor the size of the one that closed the empty half. `null` is not schema-valid for these properties and no consumer acts differently on an omitted versus null `remoteUser`, so the divergence is tolerated rather than chased. `spec: unspecified` because the spec does not define this CLI's result document at all. Tracked at #398; characterized by `wvr-readconfig-authored-empty-omitted`.

records.statement: An explicit --config pointing at a file that does not exist is rejected (no silent discovery fallback).
records.notes: both-reject agreement case: both CLIs reject an explicit --config that does not exist. Asserted directly by case-errors-decl-bad-config-path. The migrated wvr-bad-config-path record was retired 2026-08-01 — its expect was an agreement, so it tolerated no difference.

records.statement: Reading a well-formed devcontainer.json exits 0 and emits the resolved configuration as a single JSON document.

Both the `configuration` and `mergedConfiguration` documents carry `configFilePath`, an absolute VS Code URI object (`$mid`, `fsPath`, `path`, `scheme`) naming the resolved config file, whose `scheme` records HOW the file was located — `vscode-fileHost` when discovered, `file` when named with `--config`; container-only mode, which resolves no file, carries none.
records.notes: The field is a consumer-facing contract, not spec prose: a tool reading `read-configuration` output already knows how to unmarshal a VS Code URI and knows nothing about a deacon-specific alternative, so the shape is reproduced rather than reinvented. deacon emitted nothing at all, leaving every structured-output comparison reference-only on this path (75 occurrences, #376). The `scheme` is not a constant: the same path comes back as `vscode-fileHost` when the config was discovered and as `file` when it was named with `--config`. Hard-coding one of them looked right against every fixture that omits `--config` and was wrong for the two that pass it, which the live lane reported as a residual `configFilePath.scheme` divergence after the field itself was fixed. The `fsPath`/`path` split VS Code makes on Windows is deliberately NOT reproduced: it has not been observed against the pinned reference, and a guess would be a silent untested divergence rather than a visible omission. Recorded by src-obs-config-file-path.

records.statement: Configuration discovery searches exactly the three locations the spec names — `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`, `.devcontainer.json`, and `.devcontainer/<folder>/devcontainer.json` one level deep — and a plain `devcontainer.json` at the workspace root is not one of them.
records.notes: The spec's devcontainer-reference lists all three locations in precedence order. deacon searches all three; the pinned reference v0.87.0 does NOT search the one-level-deep sub-folder without an explicit --config, so it exits non-zero on a workspace whose only configuration lives there (observed 2026-07-26, src-obs-discovery-named-subfolder). Covered by a spec-expectation case pinning deacon's side and a differential recording the reference's, with wvr-discovery-named-subfolder.

records.statement: A JSON object with a duplicate top-level key is accepted with last-wins semantics, matching the reference after pruning.
records.notes: both-accept agreement case: both CLIs accept duplicate top-level JSON keys with last-wins semantics. Asserted directly by its declarative case. The migrated wvr-duplicate-keys record was retired 2026-08-01 — its expect was an agreement, so it tolerated no difference.

records.statement: A cyclic extends chain (a -> b -> a) is detected and rejected during read-configuration; the reference CLI v0.87.0 does not resolve extends and accepts.
records.notes: extends is the in-flight proposal devcontainers/spec#22 (unspecified in the pinned spec). deacon resolves eagerly and detects the loop; the reference echoes extends literally. Characterized by ext-extends-resolution and backed by case-errors-extends-cycle (issue #297). The duplicate wvr-extends-cycle record was retired 2026-08-01, leaving one characterization instead of two that could drift apart.

records.statement: read-configuration --include-merged-configuration resolves the full extends chain (base image, merged containerEnv and forwardPorts); the reference CLI v0.87.0 does not resolve extends and errors with 'No image information specified'.
records.notes: Ahead-of-spec deacon capability (devcontainers/spec#22, issue #297). Characterized by ext-extends-resolution and backed by case-tier1-extends-child. See docs/DIFFERENTIATORS.md. The duplicate wvr-extends-child-merged record was retired 2026-08-01, leaving one characterization instead of two that could drift apart.

records.statement: An extends chain pointing at a nonexistent target file is rejected during read-configuration; the reference CLI v0.87.0 does not resolve extends and accepts.
records.notes: extends is the in-flight proposal devcontainers/spec#22 (unspecified in the pinned spec). deacon resolves eagerly and errors on the missing target; the reference echoes extends literally. Characterized by ext-extends-resolution and backed by case-errors-extends-missing (issue #297). The duplicate wvr-extends-missing record was retired 2026-08-01, leaving one characterization instead of two that could drift apart.

records.statement: `--include-features-configuration` reports the resolved Feature set in install order, and a Feature supplied by `--additional-features` joins that resolution rather than being appended after it.
records.notes: Both CLIs place a dependency before its dependant, but the reported featuresConfiguration documents differ in shape: deacon reports the source identifiers, the reference additionally reports cache paths and consecutive ids that are process-local. Recorded as divergent so the difference is characterized rather than surfacing later as drift (src-obs-feature-resolution-order).

records.statement: `featuresConfiguration` is reported only when Feature resolution produced at least one Feature set; a configuration declaring no Features carries no such key, under either `--include-features-configuration` or `--include-merged-configuration`.
records.notes: deacon reported `{"featureSets": []}`, which reads as "resolution ran and produced none" where the reference says nothing at all. The value is still computed internally — the merged configuration needs it — so only what is REPORTED is filtered. Note what this behavior does NOT claim: the two CLIs agree on the flag coupling (both emit the block under `--include-merged-configuration` alone when Features exist), and the CONTENT of a non-empty `featuresConfiguration` still diverges structurally — that difference is enumerated as family (5) in the tier-1 and merged behaviors' notes and tracked in #387. Recorded by src-obs-features-configuration-empty.

records.statement: A devcontainer.json with a hard JSONC syntax error is rejected at parse rather than silently recovered; the reference CLI's recovering parser drops the broken property and accepts.
records.notes: deacon fails fast (constitution IV, no silent fallbacks); the reference is lenient at read-configuration. Backed by case-errors-malformed-json and wvr-malformed-json.

records.statement: deacon's `mergedConfiguration` omits the computed-empty properties the reference synthesizes there — `containerEnv`, `remoteEnv`, `portsAttributes` and `hostRequirements` — for a configuration that authors none of them.
records.notes: Made VISIBLE by #398, not caused by it. `mergedConfiguration` is SYNTHESIZED rather than echoed, so unlike `configuration` an empty value there is a computed default rather than authorship information. The reference materializes those defaults; deacon, having made every modeled optional skip serialization when unset, now omits them. Measured at oracle 0.87.0 for `{"image": "alpine:3.19"}`: the reference emits `remoteEnv: {}`, `containerEnv: {}`, `portsAttributes: {}` and `hostRequirements: {cpus: null, memory: "-Infinity", storage: "-Infinity"}`; deacon emits none of the four. This was previously absorbed by `drop_absent_optional`, which ran on BOTH sides of the merged block — and still does, which is why that rule survives #398 on the merged block alone. The two documents describe the same merged configuration, and the reference's `hostRequirements` values are a `Math.max()` over an empty set serialized as the strings `"-Infinity"`, which deacon should not reproduce uncritically. Recorded so the difference is characterized rather than only compensated; the compensation is scoped to the merged block and named in `normalize.rs`.

records.statement: read-configuration --include-merged-configuration over the tier1 corpus emits a merged configuration that matches the reference after normalization, except for the characterized document-shape divergences recorded below (and excluding extends, which is the deacon-extension bhv-readconfig-extends-merged).
records.notes: Backed by case-merged-corpus (parity_corpus_merged over the tier1 corpus) and by the 24 declarative merged-mode variants case-merged-decl-* (023 T039). Retiring the blanket `prune` normalizer (023 T062, research D3) surfaced previously hidden divergences against the pinned reference. Re-measured at 023 T102 over the FULL declarative run (71 cases: 20 agree, 51 diverge), counted as cases affected: (1) `configuration.configFilePath` reference-only (51 cases; also `mergedConfiguration.configFilePath`, 23); (2) `workspace.configFolderPath` and `workspace.rootFolderPath` deacon-only (51); (3) `workspace.workspaceFolder` VALUE-divergent (43); (4) the reference's merged configuration carries PLURAL command arrays (`onCreateCommands` / `postCreateCommands` / `postStartCommands` / `postAttachCommands` / `updateContentCommands`) where deacon emits only the singular forms (7-21 cases each); (5) the `featuresConfiguration` block differs in shape (`dstFolder` reference-only, `featureSets` value-divergent, 11-12); (6) `workspace.workspaceMount` VALUE-divergent (2). Families (3) and (6) were identified at T102 and are the two VALUE divergences: when the workspace folder is a SUBDIRECTORY of a git root — every in-repo fixture and every CI checkout — deacon reports `workspace.workspaceFolder` as the git ROOT's container path while the reference reports the subdirectory inside that mount, and with an explicit config `workspaceFolder` deacon renders `workspaceMount` with `target=<that folder>` where the reference uses `target=<source path>`. Both CLIs agree on the mount SOURCE, so the reference is self-consistent and deacon loses the subdirectory. This is adjacent to the documented `--mount-workspace-git-root` default, but that default governs what is MOUNTED; deriving the reported `workspaceFolder` from the mount root is a separate unintended consequence. All six are deacon-behind-reference and are tracked for FIX, not tolerated — no blanket rule was reinstated and no tolerance was authored (FR-036). See specs/023-migrate-parity-to-conformance/tasks.md#T113. STATUS: families (2), (3) and (6) are FIXED — the `workspace` section now routes through the same shared helpers `up` uses, so the host-path fields are gone, the subdirectory survives in `workspaceFolder`, and the default mount target no longer follows an explicit `workspaceFolder` (#383, and see bhv-readconfig-workspace-folder-subpath / bhv-readconfig-workspace-section-shape, which record those two claims in their own right). Families (1) and (4) are now FIXED too — `configFilePath` is emitted as the reference's URI object, and the five merged lifecycle slots are reported as `[]` when empty (see bhv-readconfig-config-file-path and bhv-readconfig-merged-lifecycle-slots). Family (5) is PARTLY fixed: the block is no longer reported as an empty container when no Feature resolves (bhv-readconfig-features-configuration-omitted-when-none), but the CONTENT of a non-empty `featuresConfiguration` still diverges structurally — the reference reports the option SCHEMA under `options` with the author's chosen values under `value`, plus staging bookkeeping (`dstFolder`, `cachePath`, `consecutiveId`, `internalVersion`, `computedDigest`) whose values are its own non-deterministic temp paths. That remainder is what keeps this behavior's `reference: divergent` status honest, and it is tracked in #387. The separate absent-optional-serialization difference (deacon emits explicit nulls where the reference omits keys) is handled by the named, enumerated `drop_absent_optional` rule and tracked at tasks.md#T111. Encoded as `spec: conformant` + `reference: divergent` + `decision: follow-spec`: deacon's RESOLUTION follows containers.dev (which does not define the read-configuration output document at all), while its output SHAPE diverges from the reference CLI's. This is not an accepted divergence — R6 forbids `align-with-reference` while actually divergent, and `intentional-divergence` would claim a deliberate choice nobody made, so the intent to align is carried here and in the tracked follow-up rather than in the decision axis.

records.statement: `mergedConfiguration` reports all five plural lifecycle hook arrays (`onCreateCommands`, `updateContentCommands`, `postCreateCommands`, `postStartCommands`, `postAttachCommands`), as `[]` when no layer contributed one; `entrypoints` is omitted when empty.
records.notes: The asymmetry is the whole content of this behavior and is measured, not assumed: on a config declaring three of the five hooks the reference emitted `updateContentCommands: []` and `postAttachCommands: []` and no `entrypoints` at all. deacon emitted a plural key only when some layer contributed a value, so an absent hook was indistinguishable from a hook the merge dropped. A single "always emit" rule would have been wrong in the other direction, which is why the flag is per-property. Recorded by src-obs-merged-lifecycle-slots.

records.statement: A workspace folder with no devcontainer configuration at all is rejected rather than resolved to an invented empty config.
records.notes: both-reject agreement case: both CLIs reject a workspace with no discoverable configuration. Asserted directly by its declarative case. The migrated wvr-missing-config record was retired 2026-08-01 — its expect was an agreement, so it tolerated no difference.

records.statement: A `portsAttributes` / `otherPortsAttributes` entry reports the keys the author wrote and no others; an unset attribute is absent rather than explicitly null.
records.notes: deacon serialized the whole `PortAttributes` struct, so a one-key entry came back with six extra explicit nulls and diverged on six paths at once. Distinct from the top-level absent-optional family (tasks.md#T111), which the harness's `drop_absent_optional` rule absorbs: that rule does not reach INTO a nested object, so this one could only be fixed at the source. Recorded by src-obs-port-attributes-authored-keys.

records.statement: Variable substitution reaches the object-shaped fields that carry user templates — `build.args`, `containerEnv`, `mounts`, and `customizations` — and a `${localEnv:VAR}` naming an unset variable resolves to the empty string rather than being left literal.
records.notes: `customizations` was the field actually missed once (#312), which is why it is named in the statement rather than left to 'object-shaped fields'. Both CLIs were observed producing identical substituted values for all four fields (src-obs-substitution-object-fields).

records.statement: Unknown / forward-compatible top-level fields are accepted and preserved verbatim in read-configuration output, matching the reference's fidelity.
records.notes: both-accept agreement case; guards against silently dropping unmodeled fields (spec extensibility model). Asserted directly by its declarative case. The migrated wvr-unknown-field-preserved record was retired 2026-08-01 — its expect was an agreement, so it tolerated no difference.

records.statement: A modelled field whose value is outside the schema's closed enum (for example `userEnvProbe: telepathy`) is rejected during configuration resolution, with a diagnostic naming the offending variant and the permitted ones.
records.notes: The pinned schema declares the enum closed, so a value outside it is not a valid configuration and deacon rejects it (constitution IV). The reference's read-configuration is a lenient parse-and-echo that accepts the value and prints it back — the divergence is the reference departing from the schema, not deacon choosing to differ from the reference. wvr-unsupported-enum-values remains, because it is what keeps the live-differential case from failing on a difference we expect to keep seeing; it records the reference's leniency, not a deacon deviation. A direction-pinning spec-expectation twin fixes which side is which.

records.statement: The reported `workspace.workspaceFolder` is the automatic source-code mount location for THIS workspace: when the workspace folder is a subdirectory of the mounted root, the path from the root down to it is preserved. The default `workspaceMount` target is `/workspaces/<basename(mount source)>` independently of `workspaceFolder`.
records.notes: devcontainerjson-reference.md defines the `workspaceFolder` default as "the automatic source code mount location", which for a workspace inside a git repository is the workspace's own path under the mounted root, not the root. deacon reported the root and used `workspaceFolder` as the mount target, so a config with an explicit `workspaceFolder` was described as mounted somewhere `up` does not mount it (`default_workspace_mount_target`, #273). Both now route through the shared helpers `up` already uses, closing #383. Recorded by src-spec-workspace-folder-default.

records.statement: The `workspace` section carries exactly `workspaceFolder` and the optional `workspaceMount`, and no other field.
records.notes: The output envelope is a reference-CLI contract, not a spec-defined shape, so `spec` is `unspecified` and the decision is to match the reference rather than to follow prose. deacon additionally emitted the host paths `rootFolderPath` and `configFolderPath`, which made every structured-output comparison diverge on two paths unrelated to the behavior under test (104 occurrences, #376). Removed rather than waived: a permanent tolerance on two fields would have hidden any future third field. Recorded by src-obs-workspace-section-shape.

records.statement: A `features` value that is a bare string instead of an object is rejected (type-strict, matching the schema shape); the reference keeps the raw JSON and accepts.
records.notes: The schema declares `features` an object; a bare string is not a valid configuration, and deacon enforces the declared shape (constitution IV) as it already did for the typed `forwardPorts`. The reference keeps the raw JSON and accepts, so the divergence is the reference not enforcing its own schema — not deacon choosing to differ. Backed by case-errors-wrong-type-features; wvr-wrong-type-features remains as the tolerance that keeps the live-differential case from failing on the reference's leniency.

records.statement: A `forwardPorts` value that is a bare string instead of an array is rejected (typed deserialization); the reference keeps the raw JSON and accepts.
records.notes: The schema declares `forwardPorts` an array; a bare string is not a valid configuration, and deacon's typed deserialization rejects it. The reference keeps the raw JSON and accepts, so the divergence is the reference not enforcing its own schema — not deacon choosing to differ. Backed by case-errors-wrong-type-forwardports; wvr-wrong-type-forwardports remains as the tolerance that keeps the live-differential case from failing on the reference's leniency.
